cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a striped indigo/magenta handwoven cotton and silk tunic (boubou/tobe) with wide sleeves and fine white chain-stitch embroidery on the chest, laid flat on a neutral background — a classic West African strip-woven gown consistent with Wolof/Senegambian tailoring traditions.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga): body flared towards the bottom by folding over the strips towards the top of the tunic, the broad sleeves longer at the top than below. Composed of narrow strips of a uniform warp-faced pattern using trans-Saharan alaari handspun magenta silk, interspersed with narrow stripes of white and indigo handspun cotton; the weft is of cotton dyed indigo. A pocket has been sewn to the front, and both front and back have been embroidered in white local silk. The embroidery is in the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern, using chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch; there is a large spiral at the front and another on the back. The knives themselves are embroidered on top of extra pieces of cloth that have been cut to shape and couched down. The tunic appears to be lined with strips of white cotton.
